channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Security in Educational Institutions for New Academic Year
item.description: Uzbekistan has implemented additional security measures in educational institutions for the new academic year. Over 5.8 million students participated in Knowledge Day events. Authorities reviewed fire safety, traffic control near schools, and inter-agency cooperation to ensure a safe learning environment.

item.title: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover reached $49.5 billion in seven months
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover for January-July 2026 reached $49.5 billion, an increase of $3.7 billion or 8.1% compared to the same period last year. Imports of machinery and transport equipment were $9.7 billion, while exports of goods, excluding gold, increased by 27.7%.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Reduce Unified Customs Duty for Individuals Starting July 2027
item.description: Starting July 1, 2027, Uzbekistan will reduce the unified customs duty for individuals importing goods for non-commercial purposes. If the calculated duty is less than the required customs fees, these fees will not be collected.

item.title: Traffic police return to regions after SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Minister thanked traffic police for their service during the SCO summit. The head of the traffic police conveyed the minister's gratitude to the personnel. Officers ensured road safety and traffic flow during the international event and will now return to their regions to resume normal duties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan sign 16 bilateral documents to boost cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and Pakistani Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif signed 16 documents to expand cooperation in trade, transit, security, education, and other areas. The agreements aim to increase mutual trade, attract investment, and include joint projects in pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and energy. Key documents include transit trade and extradition treaties.

item.title: Kazakhstan dismantles international drug network recruitment channel
item.description: Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry reported a large-scale special operation that dismantled an international channel recruiting people into a drug network. The operation, involving Ukrainian and Albanian law enforcement, Interpol, and the US DEA, lasted over a year. Criminals recruited individuals for call centers and other roles, luring them into international drug trafficking under the guise of legitimate employment.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Support Measures for Tourism Business Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced new support measures for tourism entrepreneurs, including expanded preferential lending for hotel construction and reconstruction. The decree extends subsidies for three- to five-star hotels until January 2029 and maintains tax benefits on property and land for hotels and campsites until 2030 and 2037, respectively.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans Unified Faster Payment System for Real-Time Transfers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank is developing a Faster Payment System (FPS) to enable real-time, 24/7 money transfers between individuals and legal entities. The system aims to unify various banks and payment institutions, allowing transfers via single identifiers like phone numbers or QR codes, operated by a single entity.

item.title: Tajikistan's National Bank Launches Three-Month Pilot of Digital Tax System for Individual Entrepreneurs
item.description: Tajikistan's National Bank has launched a three-month pilot phase for a digital tax platform aimed at individual entrepreneurs. The system, developed to improve tax administration and reduce administrative burdens, will be tested in a technical environment to ensure data accuracy and system stability.

item.title: Ala-Archa Glacier Loses Approximately 1.4 Meters of Ice in One Month
item.description: An expedition to Ala-Archa Gorge recorded significant ice melt, with one glacier losing about 1.4 meters in a month. Researchers installed ablation rods to measure melting intensity. The expedition also studied glacier structure, melting processes, and geomorphological changes in the Kyrgyz Republic.

item.title: India Anticipates Significant Progress in Mining Cooperation with Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have signed a memorandum on cooperation in mining and geological resources, intending to implement it. India's Ministry of External Affairs representative Sibi George stated that both sides are discussing delegation exchanges to initiate commercial projects in the mining sector. India is keen on the commercial aspects of this partnership.

item.title: Iranian President's Plane Makes Emergency Landing in Rasht Returning from Bishkek
item.description: The plane carrying Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian made an emergency landing in Rasht instead of Tehran while returning from Kyrgyzstan after attending the SCO summit. Reports from foreign media suggest the landing was prompted by air defense system activity in eastern Tehran, though no official confirmation exists.

item.title: SCO Summit in Bishkek Sends Clear Signal of Multipolar World Order, German Media Reports
item.description: The SCO summit in Bishkek sent a clear signal of a multipolar world order to Western powers, according to German publication Berliner Zeitung. The article states that the SCO is strengthening its position as an alternative model to the US-dominated international system, potentially fostering a new, stable world order.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan uses drones and cameras for online monitoring of Kyrchen Gorge
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs is using online video cameras and drones for constant monitoring of the Kyrchen Gorge, the site of the World Nomad Games. A mobile command center, 'Aska', is coordinating security personnel and information exchange in real-time to maintain public order.

item.title: Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region's energy capacity to reach 70 MW by 2025
item.description: Energy capacity in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region has significantly increased since 1991. The region's energy capacity is projected to reach 70 MW by 2025, up from 10.4 MW in 1991. Several state investment projects totaling over 700 million somoni have supported this development.

item.title: Road repairs in Naryn continue, Ministry of Transport responds to deputy
item.description: The Ministry of Transport and Communications stated that road repairs in Naryn are ongoing and denied claims of work stoppage. The ministry confirmed that 9.025 km of road base and asphalt pavement have been laid, with road markings applied to about 70% of the section. Bridge repairs are complete.

item.title: Bank of Georgia owner Lion Finance Group explores acquiring major Uzbek bank
item.description: Lion Finance Group, the owner of Bank of Georgia, is considering entering the Uzbek banking market by acquiring one of the country's leading banks. The company plans to expand Bank of Georgia's digital model to new markets, focusing on top-tier banks. Specific targets were not disclosed.

item.title: First liver and kidney transplant surgeries successfully performed in Khujand
item.description: Clinical Hospital No. 1 in Khujand, Tajikistan, has successfully performed its first liver and kidney transplant surgeries. The procedures, conducted by specialists from the National Scientific Center for Organ and Tissue Transplantation and local surgeons, were completed without complications. Both patients are reported to be in stable condition and undergoing post-operative care.

item.title: Nearly 16,000 Indian students studying in Uzbekistan, says Indian MFA
item.description: Approximately 16,000 Indian students are currently studying in Uzbekistan, primarily in medical fields, according to India's Ministry of External Affairs. Following talks between Presidents Mirziyoyev and Modi, both nations agreed to expand educational cooperation, including student exchanges and joint research. India also proposed Uzbekistan explore its GIFT City financial hub.

item.title: India's UPI payment system to launch in Uzbekistan in approximately one year
item.description: India's UPI instant payment system is expected to become operational in Uzbekistan within approximately one year. This follows the signing of a network agreement between India's NPCI International Payments Limited and Uzbekistan's HUMO payment system. The agreement will enable UPI payments across Uzbekistan via the UzQR national QR network.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India nearing agreement on long-term uranium supply
item.description: Uzbekistan and India are close to signing a new long-term agreement for uranium supply. Indian Foreign Secretary Sibi George stated that negotiations have been positive, and the deal is expected soon. Both countries also agreed to explore cooperation in geology, mining, and peaceful nuclear energy.

item.title: Tajikistan participates in World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Tajikistan is participating in the World Nomad Games held in Kyrgyzstan, where athletes from 112 countries have gathered. Further details are available.

item.title: Uzbekistan to increase cash payment limit for goods and services to 176 million soums
item.description: Uzbekistan will increase the limit for cash payments for goods and services sevenfold, to 400 BHM (176 million soums). This change is stipulated by a presidential decree aimed at implementing tasks from an open dialogue with entrepreneurs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Praised for Excellent SCO Chairmanship Performance
item.description: SCO Secretary-General Nurlan Yermekbayev stated Kyrgyzstan performed excellently as the chairing state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. He noted the country managed both leading the organization and organizing events for its 25th anniversary. Kyrgyzstan hosted over 200 events during its chairmanship, launching mechanisms for various specialized meetings.

item.title: SCO Summit Focuses on Multipolar World and Global Governance Reform
item.description: The 25th SCO summit addressed strengthening the UN's role and forming a multipolar world, aligning with the SCO's goals for global governance reform. The speech highlighted the irreversible historical process of multipolar world formation, driven by the Global South's growth, and advocated for an equitable and orderly multipolar world.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Unifying Banks into a Single Fast Payment System
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank has proposed a new regulation for a fast payment system. This system aims to enable individuals and businesses to send money in real-time, 24/7, regardless of their bank. The project seeks to create unified rules and connect various financial institutions for interoperability.

item.title: SCO Reiterates Call for Taliban to Form Inclusive Government in Afghanistan
item.description: Leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at their summit in Bishkek reiterated their call for the Taliban to form an inclusive government in Afghanistan. They stated that such a government is the only path to lasting peace, involving all ethnic and political groups. The SCO reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful, neutral Afghanistan free from terrorism and drugs.

item.title: US and Iran exchange accusations over massive strikes
item.description: The United States Central Command reported the successful completion of strikes on Iranian military targets, including IRGC facilities. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated the US attack on a residential building killed and wounded over 50 civilians. Tehran also claimed retaliatory attacks on bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Iraqi Kurdistan, and stated that many US soldiers died in an attack on Jordan.

item.title: Certain customs requirements to be canceled, export fees to decrease by 30%
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce new regulations to simplify customs procedures and enhance convenience for entrepreneurs. Starting September 1, 2026, restrictions on advance payments for imports based on invoices without foreign trade contracts will be lifted. Requirements for advance payment security for exports, including national currency transactions, will also be removed.

item.title: Official meeting between Sadyr Japarov and Shehbaz Sharif held in Bishkek
item.description: An official meeting took place in Bishkek between Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who is on an official visit. Japarov emphasized Kyrgyzstan's view of Pakistan as a reliable partner in South Asia. The leaders noted the transition from political dialogue to practical cooperation and planned to sign several documents.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to Three Years for Fighting in Russia-Ukraine War
item.description: A court in Uzbekistan's Xorazm region sentenced citizen Z.Yu. to three years in prison for fighting on the Russian side in the Russia-Ukraine war. Z.Yu. was recruited in Ufa, Bashkortostan, and received military training before being deployed to Donetsk Oblast.

item.title: Zafarabad District Governor Injured in Road Accident
item.description: The governor of Zafarabad district in Jizzakh region, Gayratjon Eshpo'latov, was involved in a road accident while in his official vehicle. Two people were in the car. The governor's condition is reported as serious.

item.title: Kyrgyz farmers sell fallen apples for low prices due to processing shortage
item.description: Farmers in Batken region, Kyrgyzstan, are selling fallen apples for 3 soms per kilogram due to a lack of processing facilities. Some apples fall from trees due to disease, affecting about 10 percent of orchards. Local residents resell these apples to Uzbekistan, where processing is more developed. Farmers have advocated for processing plants and cold storage for 20 years.

item.title: Xi Jinping attends SCO+ meeting, calls for equitable multipolar world
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping attended an SCO+ meeting, advocating for an equitable and orderly multipolar world and improved global governance. He stated that hegemonism and unilateralism are acting against historical trends, while the global majority seeks a dignified place through development and cooperation. The rise of the Global South, he noted, has made multipolarity an irreversible historical process.

item.title: Two individuals arrested in Tashkent for allegedly selling Uzbek entry visas for $31,000
item.description: Two people have been arrested in Tashkent for allegedly arranging Uzbek entry visas for foreigners for a fee. A 41-year-old man was detained while receiving $31,200 from three foreigners. He reportedly intended to give $27,000 to a 66-year-old accomplice, who was also apprehended. Criminal proceedings have been initiated.

item.title: Two individuals arrested in Tashkent for extorting $31,200 for Uzbek visas
item.description: Two people were apprehended in Tashkent for illegally obtaining $31,200 from foreign citizens in exchange for Uzbek entry visas. One individual facilitated visas for three foreigners through acquaintances, keeping $4,200 and giving $27,000 to their accomplice.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Speaker to investigate MPs' alleged involvement in land transfer to foreigners
item.description: The Speaker of the Kyrgyz Parliament, Marlen Mamataliev, will investigate allegations of parliamentary deputies' involvement in granting land to foreign entities. He stated that no law allowing land sales to China has been passed, but existing legislation permits long-term land use. New draft laws aim to strengthen restrictions on land allocation.

item.title: Zafarobod District Governor Hospitalized After Traffic Accident
item.description: The governor of Zafarobod district in Jizzakh region, Gayratjon Eshpolatov, was hospitalized in intensive care after a traffic accident involving his official car and a truck. The incident occurred on August 30. A criminal case has been initiated. The governor's son, who was driving, also sustained injuries.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imposes Three-Year Moratorium on Small Business Inspections
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has decreed a three-year moratorium on inspections of small businesses, effective August 27, 2026. Exceptions include inspections related to criminal cases, health impacts, labor law compliance, and specific citizen appeals. The Business Ombudsman will review past inspections.

item.title: New Water Supply Line in Zafarabad to Serve 400 Families
item.description: New water supply facilities have been launched in Zafarabad district, Sughd region, Tajikistan. A new drinking water line in the village of Bahoriston will initially provide clean water to 400 families, addressing long-standing water access issues. The project aims to improve living conditions and public health.
